name: Ali al-Husri al-Qayrawani
bio: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abd al-Ghani al-Fihri al-Husri was a blind poet of Kairouan and a maternal cousin of Ibrahim al-Husri, author of Zahr al-Adab. Ibn Khallikan tells that while he was still in Kairouan, al-Mu'tamid ibn Abbad of Seville sent him 500 dinars to cross the sea to him, and he declined in two lines: “You are not Noah, for your ark to save me, nor am I the Messiah, to walk on the water.” He came to al-Andalus after all, around the middle of the fifth Islamic century, when Kairouan had been ruined, and the kings of the Taifas, as Ibn Bassam puts it, passed him from one to another; he praised al-Mu'tamid and compiled an anthology for him. A master of the Quran readings, he taught them in Ceuta and elsewhere and set the reading of Nafi' in verse, and besides his diwan he left a book of elegies for a son. After the Taifa kings were deposed he settled in Tangier, where he died in 488 AH (1095 CE).
